claims.text: Conventional high-energy laser powder bed fusion of AlCrFeNiSi produces steep thermal gradients and high residual stresses.
An XGBoost-based control system can be used to optimize laser powder bed fusion process parameters.
The proposed machine-learning system will use real-time thermal feedback to continuously adjust laser power and scan speed.
Reducing instantaneous laser power and adjusting scan speed through feedback will lower applied volumetric energy density.
The intervention applies to AlCrFeNiSi miniature components with dimensions below approximately 20 mm.
A volumetric energy-density window near or slightly below 50–66.7 J/mm³ is an appropriate density-driving regime for AlCrFeNiSi.
The feedback-controlled process will produce a more uniform and controlled melt pool.
The feedback-controlled process will reduce thermal gradients.
Reduced thermal gradients will yield finer microstructural features and lower residual stresses.
Lower instantaneous power and increased scan speed will reduce peak temperatures and rapid-solidification gradients.
Reducing peak temperatures and solidification gradients will suppress residual thermal stress formation.
Reducing peak temperatures and solidification gradients will mitigate hot cracking.
The intervention will refine the microstructure and thereby improve mechanical performance.
ML-optimized AlCrFeNiSi components will have lower residual thermal stresses than components made under fixed high-thermal-load conditions.
ML-optimized AlCrFeNiSi components will exhibit greater ductility and fracture toughness than conventionally processed components.
The ML-controlled intervention will simplify the processing protocol and reduce manual intervention or post-processing.
Machine-learning models have optimized laser powder bed fusion conditions in multiple alloy systems and achieved relative density above 98%.
Existing L-PBF defect-prediction datasets include laser power, scan velocity, balling, keyholing, and lack-of-fusion information.
The benefits of ML-based process optimization demonstrated in other alloys are transferable to AlCrFeNiSi.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says processing will be simplified, but the intervention adds real-time thermal sensors, machine-learning control, continuous parameter adjustment, and acknowledged integration challenges. No operational definition explains how this more elaborate control architecture constitutes simpler processing overall.
